title: Raise automated test coverage further
description: Current unit test coverage sits around 94.6% (JaCoCo). Push further into thinly-covered areas - especially ones this QA pass had to verify manually because no test existed, like InvoiceGenerationWorker's WorkManager scheduling logic and the backup/restore file-handling paths.
acceptanceCriteria: JaCoCo coverage report identifies remaining low-coverage classes/packages
New unit tests added for BackupManager (export/stageImport/applyStaged) and InvoiceGenerationWorker's doWork() logic, which currently have no dedicated tests
Coverage gate in build.gradle.kts reviewed and raised if the new tests support it

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.

Starting - running the JaCoCo report first to see where the session's new code actually landed, then filling the named gaps (BackupManager, InvoiceGenerationWorker.doWork) before deciding whether the gate can move.

Coverage report first: this session's work had pulled the figure down to 85.3%, so the gaps this ticket names were joined by newer ones. Now 97.12% line coverage (2799/2882) with the gate raised from 0.80 to 0.93 - a few points below the measured figure, high enough that a whole feature landing untested trips it, loose enough that one uncovered branch does not block a build. One correction to the ticket's premise: BackupManager already has BackupManagerTest covering export, stageImport (including the zip-slip rejection), applyStaged and both stream-failure paths - it must have been added after this ticket was written, so no work was needed there. InvoiceGenerationWorker's doWork() IS reachable from a plain JVM test after all, with mocked Context/WorkerParameters - the exclusion claiming otherwise was wrong and is gone. New tests: InvoiceGenerationWorkerTest (bills today's agreements, skips other days, never double-bills a period, attaches pending credits), VacancyCheckWorkerTest and DuesReminderWorkerTest (both switches, the notified-set bookkeeping, the warden's threshold driving the cutoff, overdue vs future vs settled invoices, recurring vs one-off expenses), CreditRepositoryTest, ReconciliationRepositoryTest, NotificationPreferencesTest, ThemePreferencesTest, AuthPreferences pin-length round-trip and clamping, BedRepository's new aggregate queries, TenancyAgreementRepository's transferBed and setPlannedMoveOut, both new WorkScheduler jobs, and the BedFilter matcher. Exclusions rewritten to be honest rather than convenient: added only things with no JVM-reachable logic - Compose-only files (FilterChipRow, StatusBadge, AppRoot, icon sets), Migrations (raw SQL needing an instrumented MigrationTestHelper; each migration's SQL is instead diffed against Room's exported schema JSON when written), and thin Android wrappers (LodgyPdfRenderer, LodgyNotifications, HistoryCsvReader, PhotoStorage) whose logic was deliberately extracted into the testable PdfLayout/VacancyNudge/DuesNudge/HistoryCsv. To make that split real, ui/common/StatusBadge.kt was divided into StatusTokens.kt (pure level/icon/filter mapping, tested) and StatusBadge.kt (composables only, excluded). jacocoCoverageVerification passes at the new gate.

PASS. AC1: ./gradlew jacocoTestReport produces the report and it does identify the thin spots - overall LINE coverage is now 97.12% (2802 covered / 83 missed), the remaining misses being one-line synthetic lambdas and Compose helpers. AC2: both named gaps are closed - BackupManagerTest.kt has 7 tests covering export, stageImport and applyStaged, and InvoiceGenerationWorkerTest.kt has 5 tests exercising doWork(). AC3: the gate was reviewed and raised - git history shows minimum 0.80 -> 0.93, with an in-file comment explaining the choice (measured 97.1%, set a few points below so a whole untested feature trips it but one uncovered branch does not block a build). jacocoCoverageVerification passes and the full testDebugUnitTest suite is green.
